fields.description: The room this operation targets. Also the rate-limit bucket key: Google Chat allows one write per second per space.
fields.label: Room

fields.description: Per-room FIFO position. Unique with room (created by patch), which is what makes Create-Before-Edit a property of the schema rather than a hope.
fields.label: Job Sequence

fields.description: The enum IS the handler selector. Phase 2 maps it to a function through a module-level dict; the payload never carries a dotted method path, so the arbitrary-code sink the older Drive outbox has to guard against does not exist here.
fields.label: Operation
fields.options:
Message Create
Message Update
Message Delete
Space Create
Space Update
Member Add
Member Remove
Attachment Upload

fields.description: Dead means the retry budget is spent and a coworker believes they sent a message that nobody in Chat received. A daily digest surfaces Dead rows; they are not silence.
fields.label: Status
fields.options:
Pending
In Progress
Done
Failed
Dead
Skipped

fields.description: Not before this instant. Both backoff and per-space rate-limit deferral land here, so the sweeper needs exactly one ordering column.
fields.label: Available At

fields.description: The retry budget. At relay_max_attempts the row goes Dead.
fields.label: Attempts

fields.description: ONE FIELD DOING TWO JOBS, and that is the design rather than an economy. (1) It is the §4.D IN-FLIGHT CLAIM: the set of writes in flight for a room is exactly the rows with status = 'In Progress' AND lease_expires_at > now(), which is what an inbound event checks before deciding it is looking at a foreign message rather than the echo of our own POST. (2) It is the CRASHED-WORKER DETECTOR: a row still In Progress past its lease is a worker that died, and the sweeper reclaims it. No separate claims table and no Redis key - a Redis claim does not survive the deploy FLUSHDB, and during an incident it cannot be read from the desk. CLEANUP IS BY LEASE EXPIRY, NEVER BY A FINALLY BLOCK ALONE: a finally block does not run when the process is killed, which is precisely the case a lease exists for, so a claim released only in Python is a claim held forever.
fields.label: Lease Expires At

fields.description: Chat Message, Chat Room, Chat Room Member or Chat Attachment. Deliberately not indexed with reference_name: relay history for one message is an occasional admin lookup, and ordering comes from job_seq.
fields.label: Reference Document Type

fields.description: The deterministic requestId sent to Google. Deterministic so that a retry after an ambiguous timeout is de-duplicated by Google rather than by us.
fields.label: Request ID

fields.description: Which human this call is made as, under domain-wide delegation. The relay authors messages as the real person, so this is never empty for a message operation made as USER. Empty when Auth Identity is APP.
fields.label: Impersonate User

fields.description: Which Google identity this call is made as. USER is domain-wide delegation of Impersonate User - the coworker mirror, which needs a licensed Workspace account that is a joined member of the space. APP is the registered Chat app, used for Triton's own replies: no impersonation, no membership row, an App badge on the message, and Google only permits patch/delete of messages the app itself created. Decided when the job is written and frozen on the row, so a retry cannot drift to a different identity.
fields.label: Auth Identity

fields.description: Operation arguments only. Never a dotted method path - a stored callable is an arbitrary-code sink.
fields.label: Payload

fields.description: Truncated to 1000 characters at write. The writer never raises: logging must not break the action being logged.
fields.label: Last Error

fields.description: Google's canonical error status, e.g. RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED or NOT_FOUND.
fields.label: Google Error Status
